correctness.rationale: The support-functional characterization of Birkhoff orthogonality splits the polygonal unit sphere into exhaustive smooth-edge and vertex cases. For an edge interior, the unique support functional fixes the two possible unit directions of the orthogonal vector. At a vertex, all norming functionals form the convex hull of the two adjacent facet functionals, giving exactly the sign-straddling condition stated in the proof. On every resulting one-dimensional segment, both norm factors are maxima of ten affine forms; partitioning at every crossing makes their product quadratic on each cell, so endpoints and interior stationary points are exhaustive. The bundled exact checker proves the edge product bound \((63-5\sqrt5)/16\), the vertex product maximum \((2+5\sqrt5)/4\), and the explicit equality pair.
risks: The continuum extremization is computer-assisted; correctness depends on the stated affine-envelope partition being exhaustive. The checker implements exactly that finite partition rather than numerical sampling.
No claim is made for regular polygons other than the affine regular decagon.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches used the exact invariant name, Birkhoff-orthogonal formulation, regular-decagon aliases, and the candidate radical. The defining 2022 paper was inspected in full around the definition, universal bounds, examples, comparison theorem, and conclusion; it computes only the square and Hilbert cases for \(T_{\perp}\) and explicitly leaves values on further specific spaces open. A full public version of the polygonal-Radon paper was inspected for the same Birkhoff geometry, and a 2020 Radon-plane James source was inspected to the extent publicly accessible. Neither located statement covers the decagonal \(T_{\perp}\) value. The nearest exact same-invariant record is for \(\ell_3^2\), and the nearest same-space record concerns a different invariant.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent affine-regular-decagon computation could exist under different notation for \(T_{\perp}\) or as an unstated consequence of a source not retrieved in full.
The full text of the 2020 Radon-plane James paper was not publicly available through the checked route, although it predates the definition of the invariant used here.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The defining paper explicitly leaves specific-space values of the new Birkhoff constant open. The affine regular decagon is the first nonhexagonal regular \((4n+2)\)-gonal Radon plane, so it is a canonical test space for a Birkhoff-restricted invariant. The exact value is structurally informative: the global optimizer occurs at a nonsmooth vertex and strictly beats every smooth-edge Birkhoff configuration, quantifying the effect of the vertex normal cone. This is not a renaming or a routine substitution into a known formula; it requires a complete support-functional classification and exact maximization over the resulting cells.
risks: The contribution is an exact canonical benchmark rather than a classification of all polygonal Radon planes.
